average_residual.description: Average Residual Calculated by the control chart. Should always be zero

ucl3.description: Upper Control Limit 3- This is 3 standard deviations above the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid + 3 * stand_dev_resid.

standard_dev_resid.description: Standard Deviation of the Residuals calculated by the control chart.Used to calculate the control limits

lcl3.description: Lower Control Limit 3- This is 3 standard deviations below the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid - 3 * stand_dev_resid.

ucl2.description: Upper Control Limit 2- This is 2 standard deviations above the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid + 2 * stand_dev_resid.

lcl2.description: Lower Control Limit 2- This is 2 standard deviations below the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid - 2 * stand_dev_resid.

ucl1.description: Upper Control Limit 1- This is 1 standard deviations above the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid + 1 * stand_dev_resid.

lcl1.description: Lower Control Limit 1- This is 1 standard deviations below the mean and will be the value of one of the control lines in the chart in the app. Calculation: Average_Resid - 1 * stand_dev_resid.

total_violations.description: Total Number of violations found in the input dataset residuals

plot_rule1_major_outlier.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE1_MAJOR_OUTLIER' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule2_9pos_inarow.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE2_9POS_INAROW' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule3_6_trend.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE3_6_TREND' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule4_14_up_and_down.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE4_14_UP_AND_DOWN' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule7_15_stay_within_1std.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE7_15_STAY_WITHIN_1STD' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule5_2_out_of_3.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE5_2_OUT_OF_3' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule6_4_out_of_5.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE6_4_OUT_OF_5' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

plot_rule8_8stay_out_1std.description: Flags used as switches in the control chart macro to determine if violation type needs to be plotted in the chart. If so, 'PLOT_RULE8_8STAY_OUT_1STD' will be set to one, otherwise it will be zero.

model_decay_chart_cntrol_std.description: The standard deviation used to calculate the model decay metric control limits.We are still playing with this setting.

model_decay_ucl.description: Upper Control Limit for the model decay metric.This is calculated by the control chart using the model score and is based off of the Prevedere simulator data.

model_decay_lcl.description: Lower Control Limit for the model decay metric. This is calculated by the control chart using the model score and is based off of the Prevedere simulator data.

model_decay_mov_avg_n.description: The moving average setting used in the calculation of model decay.Null for usage 2 right now. This might change.

model_score2.description: The value of model_score2 that was received by the control chart macro.This is used in calculating the model MODEL_DECAY_LCL and MODEL_DECAY_UCL values.Higher scoring models have tighter expected control limits.

data_level.description: Not required for Usage two- This is the level of the data received by the control chart macro as submitted to the control chart macro.

rule1_major_outlier.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 1 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule2_9pos_inarow.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 2 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule3_6_trend.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 3 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule5_2_out_of_3.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 5 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule6_4_out_of_5.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 6 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule7_15_stay_within_1std.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 7 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

rule8_8stay_out_1std.description: Populated with the value of the residual IF rule 8 is violated.If no violation is found, the value will be missing.

name.description: The display name to be used in the application. Limited to 50 characters.

description.description: The description to be shown in the application. Limited to 1,000 characters.

color.description: The color to use in the application. Must be a valid hex color code.

category.description: The category of the indicator. Limited to 1,000 characters.

displayName.description: A user defined name for an indicator.

displayDescription.description: A user defined description for an indicator.

displayColor.description: A user defined color for an indicator. A valid six integer hex value with the leading #

displayCategory.description: A user defined category for the indicator.

offset.description: The number of periods to shift the data when modeling.

includeInModel.description: A flag used to determine if the indicator should be used when modeling.

includeInAllSegments.description:
A flag used to force the indicator in every segment. If true the indicator will be used in all segments, but may trim the model forecast to periods where data exists for the forced indicator.


Only allowed for entries with an offset of 0.

isLogged.description: A flag used to determine if the data for this indicator should be logged transformed.

transformations.description: The series transformations applied to the series of this entry and the order that they are applied

runModelHealthNow.description:
This field give the user the ability to ‘remotely press’ the ‘check model health now’ button in the app to get the latest model health results.
The default operation for this input will be to NOT ‘check model health now’. When the default value of false (don’t run model health now) is
replaced with a value of true (run model health now), the equivalent of depressing the green button in the app will be triggered.

created.description: The timestamp in UTC for when the model was created.

lastModified.description: The timestamp in UTC when the model was last saved.

owner.description: The username of the owner of the model.

companyName.description: The name of the company the model belongs to.

companyPrefix.description: The prefix of the company. A shortened name in the application which is used to differentiate between companies.

cutOffPeriods.description: The target horizon of the model. Any forecasts after the cut off periods will be trimmed.

active.description:
A flag to signal that the model is locked.


True: Model is locked and it should have a LockedModel associated with it.


False: Model is not locked and is editable in the application.

projectId.description: The UUID for the project the model is in.

usedAsIndicator.description: A flag to signal that an indicator has been created from the model.

analysisAsOfDate.description: The As Of Date of the model. This is used to front trim the model's dependent variable to use less than the full data history to run a back test or by locked models to set their coefficients to a certain model period.

logPrimary.description:
A flag which is used to determine if the primary dataset should be log(x + 1) transformed.


If this is true the calculation must be 'None'


True: Transform the points.


False: Does not transform the points.

tags.description: A list of tags that are assigned to the model.

entries.description: A list of the entries that are in the model. Includes hidden indicators as well.

url.description: The link to the model in the application.

parentType.description: The parent type of the model. Currently only parent type is a 'predict'

parentId.description: The UUID of the parent entity of the model.

parentUrl.description: The URL to the model's parent entity.

notes.description: User entered notes for the model.

modelState.description:

Draft


Archive


Production

manual.description: If true, model output was manually entered.

modelForecastSummary.description: For models in the Insights dashboard, an AI generated summary of the forecast.

tags.name: Workbench
tags.description:
Workbenches are a powerful feature in the Board Foresight application that allow users to organize and analyze data through indicators. They enable the creation of models by selecting primary and additional indicators, which can be further adjusted and managed.

Using Workbenches endpoints you can
- Retrieve the workbench information for the given workbench ID
- Update or add an indicator to the existing workbench specified by the given ID
- Retrieve the workbench series information for the given workbench ID and categories
- Retrieves the list of accessible workbenches for the company
